rows.selection_reason: With zero completed experiments, the greatest uncertainty is the absolute performance level of the simplest, most standard baseline. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the most interpretable reference: it uses the primary modality in cellular profiling (RNA), the simplest profile setting, and a well-understood linear encoder (PCA-2000). Establishing this floor is essential before evaluating whether more complex choices (learned encoders, multiprofile aggregation, image modality, or multimodal fusion) actually add value. Without a clean baseline, any subsequent performance gain or loss is uninterpretable. This single experiment maximizes information per run by anchoring the entire search space and reducing uncertainty about the starting performance level, which is the prerequisite for every later comparison.

With only one completed experiment (config_001: rna_only/singleprofile/pca_n2000 at ~48.5% acc), the dominant uncertainty is whether the image modality carries any useful signal at all. Testing image_only with resnet50 and singleprofile (config_010) isolates this fundamental question with minimal confounds. If image alone performs competitively or better than RNA alone, it strongly motivates investing subsequent budget in multimodal fusion and profile/aggregation choices. If it performs poorly, it redirects the search toward RNA encoder and multiprofile improvements, avoiding wasted experiments on multimodal configs that would likely underperform. This is the highest-information single experiment available: it partitions the remaining 50 configs into two broad strategic directions and cannot be inferred from the RNA-only baseline.

Evidence: config_001 (RNA-only, singleprofile, PCA-2000) achieves 48.5% acc, while config_010 (image-only, ResNet50) is near-random at 20.8%, indicating RNA is the dominant signal and image contributes little standalone. With only two data points, the most important uncertainty is whether the RNA encoder choice is a meaningful design axis. Question tested: config_004 (RNA-only, singleprofile, scvi_n200) is a controlled comparison to config_001 that changes only the RNA encoder from a linear method (PCA) to a learned nonlinear autoencoder (scVI, 200-dim latent). This isolates whether a structured, biologically-informed representation can outperform variance-maximizing PCA. Why this is the best next experiment: it is the minimal, highest-information change from our current best result. If scVI improves accuracy, it validates learned encoders and justifies further investment in encoder choice (e.g., scGPT) and multimodal fusion with a stronger RNA backbone. If it does not improve, it tells us PCA already captures the relevant variance and the bottleneck lies elsewhere (task difficulty, profile strategy), redirecting budget toward multiprofile aggregation or fusion strategies rather than encoder upgrades.

Evidence: scvi_n200 (acc 0.5203) outperforms pca_n2000 (0.4849) in singleprofile RNA-only, indicating learned representations matter. Image-only is very weak (0.2079), so the RNA branch is clearly the primary signal source. Uncertainty: We have zero data on whether multiprofile aggregation adds value over singleprofile—this is an entirely untested design dimension. This experiment (config_005: rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) extends our best RNA encoder to the multiprofile setting with the simplest aggregation (avgpool), isolating the effect of multi-profile information. If it improves over 0.5203, multiprofile is a productive direction and we can next test transformer aggregation; if it does not, we save budget by avoiding further multiprofile experiments and can pivot to scgpt or multimodal fusion. This is the highest-information single experiment under the limited budget because it resolves the largest open design question (single vs. multi-profile) using the encoder with the strongest prior evidence.

Evidence: config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) is the strongest result at 0.650 acc, showing multiprofile + scvi_n200 is a clear winning combination. However, the aggregation method is a completely untested dimension — we only have one data point (avgpool). Question: Does transformer aggregation outperform avgpool for the best RNA multiprofile setup? This is a clean single-variable change from config_005, making the result highly interpretable. Why this is the best next experiment: (1) It directly exploits the strongest direction found so far by testing a logical extension. (2) It reduces uncertainty about a critical design choice (aggregation) that will govern all future multimodal experiments — if transformer helps, it signals a new axis of improvement; if not, we confirm avgpool sufficiency and redirect budget toward multimodal fusion or encoder alternatives. (3) With a limited budget, resolving this question before launching into the 36 multimodal configurations avoids committing to a suboptimal aggregation strategy across many expensive multimodal runs.

The strongest finding so far is the large jump from single-profile to multi-profile with scVI n200 (0.520 → 0.650), while aggregation method (avgpool vs transformer) made negligible difference. However, we have no evidence that this multi-profile benefit generalizes beyond scVI. Config_002 (PCA n2000, multi-profile, avgpool) is a clean single-variable extension of config_001 (PCA n2000, single-profile, 0.485): it isolates whether the multi-profile structural gain is encoder-agnostic or specific to scVI's learned representation. If multi-profile PCA also improves substantially, it confirms multi-profile as the dominant design lever and justifies broad investment across encoders. If it stays near 0.485, it reveals that scVI's latent structure is necessary for multi-profile to be effective, sharply narrowing the search to scVI-based configurations. This is the highest-information-per-experiment choice under the limited budget because it resolves the key uncertainty about whether to optimize encoder choice or profile structure first.

Evidence: The best RNA-only setup so far is multiprofile + scvi_n200 + transformer (config_006, acc=0.653), and scvi_n200 consistently outperforms pca_n2000 across both profile settings. However, scgpt is entirely untested, leaving a critical uncertainty about whether a third encoder could substantially improve the RNA signal before we commit budget to multimodal fusion experiments. Question: Does scgpt match or exceed scvi_n200 under the same multiprofile + transformer conditions? This is a clean 1-factor comparison (encoder) against config_006. Why this is the best next step: The RNA encoder is the most fundamental design choice—it determines the quality of the primary signal in every downstream multimodal experiment. Resolving whether scgpt is competitive (or superior) before testing multimodal fusion avoids wasting limited budget on multimodal configs built on a suboptimal encoder. If scgpt ≈ scvi_n200, we confirm the current best and pivot to multimodal; if scgpt is markedly better, we redirect the multimodal search toward scgpt-based configs.

Evidence: The best RNA-only result is scvi_n200 + multiprofile + transformer (0.653 acc, config_006), and image-only resnet50 single-profile is very weak (0.208 acc, config_010). The critical open question is whether adding the image modality to the strongest RNA pipeline yields any complementary signal, or whether the weak image performance (0.208) means fusion will be neutral-to-harmful. Config_032 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, concat) directly tests this by taking the proven best RNA configuration and adding image with the simplest fusion (concat). This is the most informative next step because: (1) it exploits the strongest known RNA setup, (2) it answers the highest-uncertainty design question—does multimodal help at all in this task—before spending budget on more complex fusion variants or alternative image encoders, and (3) the result will determine whether subsequent experiments should invest in multimodal exploration (ViT, weighted fusion) or refocus on RNA-only refinements.

The current best is config_032 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, concat) at 0.688 acc. The image-only baseline was very weak (0.208), suggesting the image modality contributes limited signal and may benefit from reweighting rather than equal-weight concatenation. Config_033 is a direct controlled comparison to config_032, changing only fusion from concat to weighted. This isolates the fusion-strategy question: does the image branch need to be down-weighted relative to the RNA branch, or are the features complementary enough that simple concatenation suffices? Under a limited budget, this single-variable test reduces uncertainty about an important design decision (how to combine modalities) without confounding other factors (encoder, aggregation, profile setting all held constant at their best-known values). The result will directly inform whether to invest further in multimodal configurations and, if weighted fusion wins, which modality to trust more.

The current best configuration (config_033, acc 0.713) uses scvi_n200 + resnet50 + transformer + weighted fusion in a multimodal multiprofile setting. The image encoder dimension is completely unexplored in multimodal fusion—only resnet50 has been tested, and image-only resnet50 performed very poorly (0.208), suggesting the image signal may be underutilized. Config_039 swaps in imagenet_vit_l while keeping all other settings at their empirically best values (scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer, weighted). This directly tests whether a stronger, higher-capacity image encoder can improve the multimodal contribution. It is the most informative next step because: (1) it isolates the image encoder variable against the strongest known baseline, (2) it exploits the evidence that weighted fusion and transformer aggregation are beneficial, and (3) the answer—whether ViT-L helps or not—will clarify whether further investment in the image modality is worthwhile or whether the RNA modality is already capturing most of the signal. Under a limited budget, this single experiment resolves a major unexplored design axis while building on the most promising configuration.
